stories.title: Death toll from Indonesia earthquake climbs to 68 — Reuters
stories.summary: TOKYO, August 17. The death toll from a magnitude 7.7 earthquake that struck Indonesia’s East Nusa Tenggara on Saturday has risen to 68, Reuters reported, citing the Asian republic’s National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB). According to Antara news agency, BNPB earlier recorded at least 199 injuries from the quake, with almost 10,000 people forced to evacuate. A powerful earthquake struck off Flores Island in eastern Indonesia on August 15. As many as 2,400 houses, dozens of educational facilities, places of worship and government offices were damaged. More than 5,400 locals are staying in centralized evacuation shelters. The republic has sent 52 metric tons of aid to those affected. Earlier, the Russian embassy in Indonesia offered condolences over the death toll and damage on its Telegram channel.

stories.headline: Hong Kong halves environmental impact review times with AI in efficiency drive

opening: Hong Kong authorities have slashed the time required for environmental impact assessments by up to half using artificial intelligence (AI), as part of flagship initiatives in the first batch of projects aimed at enhancing efficiency.

The first batch of 30 projects, involving 13 government departments, was announced on Monday, covering transport and food business licensing, leisure and sports facilities, environmental hygiene, complaint handling, and environmental protection.

stories.title: Consultation ending on controversial Rosebank oil field
stories.summary: Supporters and opponents of the controversial Rosebank oil field have been making their cases as a consultation on the plans draws to a close. The industry regulator is considering revised applications for the £8.7bn project off Shetland and the Jackdaw gas field after a court ruled that they had been unlawfully approved. But the boss of oil company Adura, CEO Neil McCulloch, says fossil fuels will be needed for years to come and that producing them domestically will generate billions in tax revenues. McCulloch said he was confident there was a "balance of advantages" in approving Rosebank and added: "The ball is back now in the government's court." Isobel Reid from Uplift has called on the government to reject the applications, insisting that more drilling will "wreck our planet" and result in more extreme weather. "The prime minister must take urgent steps to deal with the root of the problem - burning fossil fuels is what feeds climate change," she said. The Rosebank oil field and the Jackdaw gas field, 150 miles east of Aberdeen, had been approved under the previous Conservative government and construction is well under way. A legal challenge was brought at the Court of Session in Edinburgh in 2024 which argued that consent was given without fully considering the impact of burning the fossil fuels which will be produced. The previous decisions were ruled unlawful and sent back to the regulator Opred to be taken again. The judge ruled that the operators could continue preparatory work at the sites but must stop short of producing oil and gas until a final decision had been taken. Rosebank is estimated to contain the equivalent of up to 300 million barrels of oil and at its peak will produce approximately 69,000 barrels a day. Most of that is oil which will be shipped to Europe for refining before being sold on the open market.
